patients.summary: Disabled former construction worker and heavy smoker with COPD, hypertension, CAD and lithium-treated bipolar I who joins in 2021. Over the next five years he is treated for a tongue cancer with nodal spread, develops lithium nephrotoxicity, and survives a COPD admission, a metoprolol overdose, massive hemoptysis and a refractory VF arrest that ends with an ICD.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

54M transferring from a practice he went to for years; records requested 8/30, not here yet. Brought a grocery bag of bottles, which helped.

Worked construction for years as a framer and then a site foreman; on disability now. Married, lives in Sunderland with his wife.

Problems as he and the bottles tell it:
- COPD. Told years ago he has "the start of emphysema" based on symptoms; he does not remember a breathing test. On tiotropium HandiHaler daily. Short of breath on hills and carrying lumber for his own projects, morning cough most days. No hospital stays for his lungs.
- HTN on four agents: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 25, metoprolol tartrate 50 BID.
- CAD, called stable on the old list. He is vague on details and has not seen a heart doctor in years. Aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40 at night. No exertional chest pain.
- Bipolar I. Lithium 300 mg TID for about ten years, prescribed by his psychiatrist, whom he sees every few months. No episodes in a long time, no hospitalizations in that span. Gets his levels drawn through psychiatry, he thinks.
- Smoking: started at 17, a pack a day ever since, about 40 pack-years. Not ready to set a quit date; willing to talk about it again.

Alcohol: a beer or two on weekends. No drug use.
Allergies: none to medications.
Surgeries: none he can name.
Family: father had an MI at 62 and high blood pressure. Mother had emphysema and died at 70. One brother with bipolar disorder.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing, smells of smoke. Oropharynx without lesions. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs with diminished breath sounds throughout and a prolonged expiratory phase, no wheeze today. Abdomen soft. No leg edema. Affect bright, speech normal rate, linear.

A/P
1. COPD on LAMA, clinical label only. Spirometry would be nice; will see what the old records hold first.
2. HTN at goal on current four drugs, no change.
3. CAD, stable. Continue aspirin, statin, beta blocker. Lipids today.
4. Bipolar I on lithium. CMP, TSH and lithium level today; I will ask psychiatry to copy us on levels.
5. Tobacco: meets criteria for annual low-dose CT. Ordered. Brief counseling, he knows.
6. Screening: hep C and HIV once, both today. Colonoscopy he says was done a few years back, normal.

RTC 3 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sean, your labs from yesterday are back. Kidney function, salts, liver tests and blood counts are fine. Lithium level is in the target range, thyroid normal, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. Cholesterol is reasonable on the atorvastatin. Nothing to change. The lung scan order went to scheduling, they will call you.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
62 pages received by fax from the prior primary care office. Abstracted for PCP:
- Problem list there: COPD, hypertension, CAD, bipolar disorder, tobacco use. COPD entered on clinical grounds; no PFT report anywhere in the packet. No cardiology letters or stress test reports included.
- Med list matches what he brought in.
- Colonoscopy 2018, outside GI: normal exam, no polyps, 10-year repeat.
- Immunizations: Pfizer COVID doses 3/19/21 and 4/9/21 entered. No pneumococcal or shingles vaccines on file. Flu shots most years, no lot info.
- Labs 2019 to 2021: creatinine 0.9 to 1.1, lithium levels drawn by psychiatry not included.
Scanned to Media. PCP to review.

reports.text:
TECHNIQUE: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast.
COMPARISON: None.
FINDINGS: No pulmonary nodules. Airways patent. No consolidation or effusion. Heart size normal. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: No nodules. Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

Three-month check. Feels about the same. Breathing his usual; uses the HandiHaler every morning. Got a Moderna booster at the pharmacy last month, he thinks. Mood steady, saw psychiatry in November.
Still a pack a day. We talked about varenicline and patches; he wants to get through the holidays first.

BP and pulse fine today. Lungs quiet with long expirations, no wheeze. No edema.

Plan: no changes. BMP and lithium level today since we are not getting psych's draws. Next visit spring. Booster dose to be entered once the pharmacy record shows up.

MEDICARE AWV (initial)

Health risk assessment reviewed with patient. Lives with wife, two-story house, manages his own pills with a weekly box. No falls. Hearing ok. Drives. Advance directive: has not done one, wife would be his decision-maker; packet given.

Interval: no ED visits. Breathing unchanged. Mood stable per him and psych.

Exam: vitals as charted. Mouth and throat clear. No cervical or supraclavicular nodes. Heart RRR. Lungs diminished, long expiration. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without concerning lesions. Gait steady. PHQ-9 2.

Prevention:
- Colonoscopy 2018 normal, next 2028.
- LDCT due October, ordered.
- Tdap today (none on record). Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2 to 6 months.
- PCV20 done last fall.
- Moderna booster from 11/2021 entered from pharmacy record.
- Hep C and HIV done 2021.

Tobacco: ~5 min counseling. Precontemplative, says "it's who I am." Door left open.

Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids, TSH, lithium, UA.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza IM left arm, Pfizer bivalent IM right arm. Screening questions negative. Tolerated, observed 15 min. Reminded him Shingrix #2 is due next month, booked for 10/25.

events.reason: Worsening cough and shortness of breath

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: progressive cough and dyspnea in COPD without spirometry on file

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rebooked from the December no-show.

CC: breathing.
HPI: Since late summer the cough has been more days than not, with more breathlessness on stairs and walking out to the mailbox in the cold. Used to get winded on hills only. No fever, no sweats at night, weight steady per our scale. No blood in the sputum. Using the tiotropium daily, technique looks right when he shows me. Still 1 ppd.

Exam: vitals as charted. Not in distress, speaks full sentences. Chest: diminished air movement both sides, prolonged expiratory phase, no crackles. Heart regular. No clubbing, no edema.

A/P: COPD by history, symptoms progressing over roughly 4 to 5 months. He has never had spirometry. Referring to pulmonology for PFTs and to sort out next steps on inhalers. Asked him again about quitting; he says he will "think about it after the lung doctor yells at me."

events.reason: Persistent cough and shortness of breath

medications.drug: NDA020983 60 ACTUAT albuterol 0.09 MG/ACTUAT Metered Dose Inhaler
medications.sig: Inhale 2 puffs every 4 to 6 hours as needed for shortness of breath or wheeze

reports.text: PA and lateral views. The lungs are hyperinflated and both hemidiaphragms are flattened. No focal consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Cardiomediastinal silhouette within normal limits. Osseous structures intact.
reports.conclusion: Hyperinflation with flattened diaphragms. No acute process.

reports.text: Pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry with lung volumes. Acceptable and reproducible efforts. FEV1/FVC ratio is reduced, consistent with airflow obstruction. Total lung capacity is within normal limits.
reports.conclusion: Obstructive ventilatory defect with normal total lung capacity, consistent with COPD.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONARY ASSOCIATES — CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 03/17/2023
Referring: primary care physician

Thank you for sending Mr. Finn, a 56-year-old man with a clinical COPD label, for evaluation of half a year of increasing cough and breathlessness. He reports no fevers, no night sweats and no weight loss.

Current medications: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, metoprolol tartrate 50 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, lithium 300 mg TID, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: active smoker, roughly 1 pack daily, about 40 pack-years. Rare alcohol.
Family: mother with emphysema.

Exam: BP 135/85, HR 78, SpO2 92% on room air at rest. Barrel-shaped chest. Breath sounds decreased bilaterally with a prolonged expiratory phase. No clubbing.

Data: Hgb 15.0, WBC 7.0, platelets 250. Na 140, K 4.2, creatinine 1.0.
CXR today: hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, nothing acute.
PFTs today: reduced FEV1/FVC, normal TLC.

Impression: COPD, now confirmed by spirometry. Ongoing tobacco use is the main driver.

Recommendations:
1. Continue tiotropium daily.
2. Albuterol HFA 2 puffs q4-6h as needed, prescription sent.
3. Smoking cessation strongly advised; offered pharmacotherapy, he declined for now.
4. Vaccines appear current per patient.
5. Return to pulmonary clinic as needed or with any exacerbation.

CC: primary care

documents.title: rescue inhaler
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The lung doctor gave me an albuterol. Pharmacy says its covered but the brand he wrote costs me more. Can you send the cheaper one?

documents.title: RE: rescue inhaler
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Spoke with the pharmacist, they can substitute the covered albuterol inhaler with no new prescription needed. Should be $0 with your MassHealth. Call us if it is not.

orders.reason: firm 3 cm left cervical lymph node in a heavy smoker

documents.title: Same-day visit: neck lump
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted this morning about a lump; seen same day.

Noticed a bump on the left side of his neck shaving about three weeks ago. Thinks it is a little bigger. It does not hurt. No sore throat, no recent cold or dental infection, no fevers, eating normally, weight unchanged.

Exam: left cervical chain with a single firm, non-tender node about 3 cm, not fixed to skin, skin over it normal. No other cervical, supraclavicular, axillary nodes. Oral cavity looked unremarkable to my eye with a light, though I am not the right person to examine the back of his mouth thoroughly. Lungs his baseline.

A/P: Persistent firm 3 cm neck node in a 56-year-old pack-a-day smoker is cancer until proven otherwise; told him that plainly, he appreciated it. Urgent referral to the head and neck clinic at the outside hematology/oncology group for scope and tissue. CBC today. I will call the clinic myself to move it up.

documents.title: Urgent referral
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Called the head and neck intake line, faxed note and CBC. Their first new-patient opening is June 19; placed on cancellation list. Pt informed, he will keep his phone on.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of border of tongue
conditions.note: left lateral border; primary for the nodal disease

conditions.label: Secondary malignant neoplasm of lymph nodes of head, face and neck
conditions.note: left cervical node, FNA squamous cell carcinoma

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Fine needle aspiration, left cervical lymph node.
ADEQUACY: Satisfactory for evaluation.
MICROSCOPIC: Smears and cell block show clusters of atypical squamous cells with keratinization in a background of necrosis and lymphoid cells.
reports.conclusion: Left cervical lymph node, FNA: positive for malignant cells, consistent with squamous cell carcinoma.

documents.title: Head and Neck Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY — HEAD AND NECK CLINIC
Visit date: 06/19/2023

Reason for referral: left neck mass.

HPI: 56-year-old man, active smoker, about 40 pack-years, who first felt a lump on the left neck roughly 2 months ago. It has grown slowly and is painless. He denies a recent infection, fevers and weight loss. He was seen by pulmonology this spring for COPD.

PMH: COPD, hypertension, CAD, bipolar I disorder on lithium.
Meds: per referral, including lithium 300 mg TID and tiotropium.
Allergies: none known.

Exam: Left cervical chain: firm, non-tender node about 3 cm; no overlying skin change. No other adenopathy appreciated. Flexible fiberoptic laryngoscopy: a small ulcerated lesion along the left lateral tongue border. Remaining oropharyngeal mucosa, larynx and hypopharynx appear normal.

Procedure: ultrasound-guided FNA of the left neck node performed today. Cytology (final 6/22): squamous cell carcinoma.

Assessment: squamous cell carcinoma of the left lateral oral tongue with left cervical nodal metastasis.

Plan:
- Staging PET-CT.
- Presented at multidisciplinary tumor board once staging is back; anticipated surgery with partial glossectomy and left neck dissection, likely followed by radiation.
- Dental evaluation before any radiation.
- Smoking cessation: discussed its effect on healing and outcomes.

CC: primary care physician

documents.title: Call with patient after FNA result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pt texted that the oncology team called with the biopsy: squamous cell cancer. Called him back. His wife on speaker. They understand the tongue spot is where it started and the node is spread to the neck. Questions answered in general terms; told them the head and neck team is the right place for treatment specifics. Offered a video visit once the scan is done to go over the plan together. Checked on mood: scared but sleeping, no racing thoughts, taking lithium. Wife will call if anything changes.

reports.text:
INDICATION: Newly diagnosed squamous cell carcinoma, left oral tongue with left cervical nodal metastasis. Staging.
TECHNIQUE: FDG PET with low-dose CT from skull base to mid-thigh. Fasting glucose acceptable.
FINDINGS:
Head and neck: FDG-avid focus along the left lateral oral tongue corresponding to the known primary. Single FDG-avid left level II lymph node measuring about 3 cm in short axis. No contralateral or other cervical nodal uptake.
Chest: no FDG-avid pulmonary nodules or mediastinal or hilar nodes.
Abdomen and pelvis: physiologic distribution. No suspicious uptake.
Bones: no suspicious osseous uptake.
reports.conclusion: FDG-avid left lateral tongue primary and single left level II nodal metastasis. No distant metastatic disease.

documents.title: Outside PET-CT received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Staging PET from the oncology group's imaging center scanned in: tongue primary and one left level II node, nothing in the chest or beyond. Video visit already booked for next week.

events.reason: Review of cancer diagnosis and treatment plan

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at home with wife, consented. 25 min.

Went through the PET together: one node, the tongue primary, no spread to lungs or elsewhere. Tumor board recommendation as they heard it: surgery on 7/26 (part of the tongue plus the left neck nodes) and then probably radiation. Dental clearance done last week.

Medical prep: he asked if he needs to stop anything. Told him the surgical team will give instructions; usually aspirin decisions come from them and I am fine with whatever they choose. Lithium: anesthesia and surgery should know he is on it; asked them to keep hydrated and check a level if he is NPO long. Sent a summary letter to the surgeon's office with his med list.

Mood: anxious but steady. PHQ not repeated today. No changes to lithium; psychiatrist aware.

Tobacco: still smoking. The team has asked him to stop for healing; offered help any time he wants it.

events.reason: Partial glossectomy and left neck dissection

reports.text:
SPECIMENS: A. Left lateral tongue, partial glossectomy. B. Left neck, selective dissection levels I to IV.
A. Invasive squamous cell carcinoma, keratinizing, moderately differentiated. Greatest dimension 1.4 cm. Depth of invasion 4 mm. All margins negative for carcinoma.
B. Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in 1 of 22 lymph nodes (level II), 3.0 cm. No extranodal extension.
reports.conclusion: Squamous cell carcinoma of the left lateral tongue, 1.4 cm, depth of invasion 4 mm, margins negative; 1/22 lymph nodes positive, 3.0 cm, no extranodal extension. pT1 N1.

documents.title: Discharge Summary, Head and Neck Surgery
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — OTOLARYNGOLOGY / HEAD AND NECK SURGERY
Admit 07/26/2023, discharge 07/28/2023

Diagnosis: squamous cell carcinoma of the left lateral oral tongue with a single left cervical nodal metastasis.
Procedure 07/26: left partial glossectomy with primary closure and left selective neck dissection (levels I to IV). Drain placed.

Course: Uneventful. Clear liquids on day 1, soft diet by day 2. Drain removed on day 2. Pain controlled on acetaminophen. Home medications resumed, lithium level checked on day 1 and in range, aspirin held 5 days before surgery and restarted at discharge.

Pathology (final 08/01): 1.4 cm keratinizing SCC, depth of invasion 4 mm, margins clear; 1 of 22 nodes positive (level II, 3.0 cm), no extranodal extension. pT1 N1.

Disposition: home with wife. Follow up in clinic in 10 days. Referred to radiation oncology for adjuvant treatment given nodal disease.

Discharge medications: unchanged from admission list.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Check-in after surgery
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called to check in after the 7/26 surgery; discharge summary is in the chart. Neck incision healing, saw the surgeon last week, stitches out. Eating soft foods. Pain controlled with Tylenol. Radiation planning visit is next week. Taking all his usual pills including lithium. No questions for PCP.

documents.title: Radiation Oncology Treatment Summary
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
RADIATION ONCOLOGY — END OF TREATMENT SUMMARY

Diagnosis: pT1 N1 squamous cell carcinoma, left oral tongue, status post partial glossectomy and left selective neck dissection 07/26/2023, margins negative, no extranodal extension.
Intent: adjuvant.
Treatment: IMRT to the tumor bed and left neck, 60 Gy in 30 fractions, 09/05/2023 to 10/17/2023. No concurrent chemotherapy.
Course: completed as planned without treatment breaks.
Follow-up: head and neck surveillance with the oncology group every 3 months for the first year; post-treatment PET-CT about 12 weeks after completion. Annual TSH recommended after neck radiation.

CC: primary care, head and neck surgery, medical oncology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First time in person since the surgery and radiation. Finished radiation 10/17, end-of-treatment summary received. Eating soft foods, speech clear to me. PET planned in January by the oncology group.

Breathing: no change from his usual, using albuterol maybe twice a week. Still smoking a pack a day, which he volunteered with some embarrassment.

Mood steady, sleeping.

Exam: vitals charted. Healed left neck incision. Lungs diminished with prolonged expiration. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P:
- Tongue SCC s/p surgery and adjuvant RT, in surveillance with oncology.
- After neck radiation, TSH yearly; drawn today with lithium level and BMP.
- COPD stable.
- Tobacco: 1 ppd. Talked about varenicline again; he will think about it.
- Flu and updated COVID given.

documents.title: Kidney number
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sean, thyroid and lithium level are fine. Your kidney number (creatinine) came back 1.5, up from about 1.0 in the spring. Could be from not drinking much during radiation, but lithium can also affect the kidneys over time. Please drink normally, avoid ibuprofen or naproxen, and let's recheck in about 2 months. The lab order is in.

documents.title: Head and Neck Surveillance Visit
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
HEAD AND NECK CLINIC — FOLLOW-UP
Visit 12/05/2023

Seven weeks out from adjuvant IMRT for pT1 N1 left oral tongue SCC. Swallowing soft solids, weight stable.
Exam: surgical site of the left lateral tongue well healed, no mucosal lesion. Neck soft, no palpable adenopathy. Flexible laryngoscopy: no lesions.
Impression: no clinical evidence of disease.
Plan: PET-CT in early January; return 3 months. Continue to encourage smoking cessation.

CC: primary care

reports.text:
INDICATION: pT1 N1 left oral tongue SCC, status post partial glossectomy, left neck dissection and adjuvant radiation completed 10/17/2023. Response assessment.
COMPARISON: PET-CT 07/05/2023.
FINDINGS: Postsurgical and post-radiation changes of the left oral tongue and left neck without focal FDG avidity. No FDG-avid cervical lymph nodes. No FDG-avid pulmonary nodules or thoracic adenopathy. No suspicious abdominal, pelvic or osseous uptake.
reports.conclusion: Expected post-treatment changes. No evidence of residual or recurrent disease.

documents.title: Outside PET-CT received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Post-treatment PET from the oncology group: no evidence of disease. Good news; he already heard it from them. Filed.

documents.title: Creatinine trend
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine now 1.8, after 1.5 in November and about 1.0 for years before that. Urine without protein or blood. Lithium level in range. Not explained by radiation-era dehydration anymore. Asked front desk to bring him in this week to talk about nephrology.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: creatinine 1.0 to 1.8 over 10 months on long-term lithium

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the kidney labs.

Creatinine 1.0 (Mar 2023), 1.5 (Nov), 1.8 (last week). UA bland. Lithium levels have stayed in range. Takes no NSAIDs, he says, only Tylenol for the occasional ache. Drinks plenty of coffee, "some water." Feels fine apart from his breathing.

On lisinopril and HCTZ along with lithium, both of which can push lithium levels and kidney numbers.

Exam: BP and HR as charted. No edema. Lungs at baseline.

A/P: Progressive decline in kidney function on a decade of lithium. Needs nephrology input, and any change to lithium goes through his psychiatrist. Referral placed. Kept everything else the same for now pending their advice. Encouraged water through the day.

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEPHROLOGY GROUP — NEW CONSULTATION
Date of service: 03/18/2024

Reason: declining renal function in a patient on long-term lithium.

HPI: 57-year-old man treated with lithium for bipolar I disorder for roughly ten years, with no mood episodes in recent memory. He describes more tiredness lately and getting up to urinate more often, including at night. COPD, hypertension, CAD; treated this past year for a left oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma with surgery and radiation.

Medications: lithium carbonate 300 mg TID, lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metoprolol tartrate 50 mg BID, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, tiotropium, albuterol as needed.
Allergies: none known.
Social: smokes about a pack a day; light alcohol.

Exam: BP 130/85. No peripheral edema.

Labs today: creatinine 2.1, BUN 35, serum lithium 1.2 (within the therapeutic range). Urinalysis negative for protein and blood.
Primary care trend: creatinine about 1.0 in 2023, 1.5 in 11/2023, 1.8 in 01/2024.

Assessment: chronic kidney injury most consistent with lithium nephrotoxicity.

Plan:
1. Discussed lithium with his psychiatrist by phone. Given ten years of stability on it, the shared decision is to continue lithium for now.
2. Serum lithium and BMP every 3 months; primary care to draw.
3. Avoid NSAIDs. Maintain good fluid intake.
4. Return to nephrology in 6 to 12 months or sooner if creatinine rises further.

CC: primary care, outpatient psychiatry

documents.title: kidney doctor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw the kidney doctor last week. He says the lithium is what is doing it but we are staying on it and you are supposed to check it every 3 months. Did he send you anything?

documents.title: RE: kidney doctor
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Nothing yet from nephrology. We requested the note today. Your doctor will set up the 3-month labs at your April visit.

documents.title: Call to outpatient psychiatry
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Still no nephrology letter. Called his psychiatrist's office and spoke with the psychiatrist. Confirms the conversation with nephrology and the plan to continue lithium 300 TID for now, with levels every 3 months. Agreed we will draw them here and fax results to psychiatry. They do not routinely send notes; asked them to call if they change the dose.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Nephrology letter came in yesterday. Creatinine 2.1 there, BUN 35, lithium 1.2, urine bland. Their read is lithium nephrotoxicity, and with psychiatry they are keeping lithium. The lab-calculated eGFR on that creatinine is in the 3b range, so CKD 3b on the list.

He is still up at night to pee, tired some afternoons. Mood good.

Exam: BP fine. No edema.

Plan:
- Standing BMP + lithium q3 months here, results faxed to psychiatry.
- No NSAIDs, reinforced. He knows Tylenol is the safe one.
- Antihypertensives unchanged.
- Next draw June.

GENERAL SURGERY CLINIC
DOS 09/23/2024

Referred for a right inguinal hernia. Reducible, mildly symptomatic with lifting.

PMH: COPD, HTN, CAD, bipolar I on lithium, CKD from lithium, oral tongue SCC treated 2023 (NED).
Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 25, metoprolol tartrate 50 BID, lithium 300 TID, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, tiotropium, albuterol.
NKDA.
Smoking: currently one pack daily.

Exam: BP 138/82, HR 78, SpO2 96% RA. Lungs with mild expiratory wheezes on both sides. Abdomen soft, reducible right inguinal hernia, no tenderness.

Labs: Hgb 14.2, WBC 7.2, plt 250, fasting glucose 98, creatinine 1.9 (known CKD).

Plan: open right inguinal hernia repair with mesh as an outpatient. Because he still smokes, strongly advised stopping before surgery to lower wound and pulmonary risk; nicotine patch 21 mg daily prescribed. Aspirin may continue. Anesthesia aware of lithium and COPD. Tentative date 10/30.

CC: primary care

documents.title: Flu and COVID vaccines

AMBULATORY SURGERY CENTER — OPERATIVE REPORT
Date: 10/30/2024
Preoperative and postoperative diagnosis: right inguinal hernia.
Procedure: open right inguinal hernia repair with polypropylene mesh (Lichtenstein technique).
Anesthesia: general with local infiltration.
Findings: indirect hernia sac, reduced; cord structures preserved; ilioinguinal nerve identified and protected.
EBL minimal. No complications. Discharged home the same day in good condition.
Follow-up: surgical clinic in 2 weeks. No lifting over 10 lb for 4 weeks.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 03/16/2025 10:15

CC: a week of more shortness of breath and a productive cough.

58M with COPD on tiotropium, active smoker, treated oral cavity cancer, CKD, bipolar on lithium. Increasing dyspnea and sputum for about 7 days, worse overnight.
Home meds per patient: tiotropium, metoprolol, lisinopril, amlodipine, HCTZ, lithium, aspirin, atorvastatin. NKDA. Smoking roughly 40 pack-years.

Triage: BP 150/90, HR 88, RR 22, SpO2 89% on room air.
Exam: diffuse wheezing with a prolonged expiratory phase. No leg swelling.
ABG on room air: pH 7.32, PaCO2 55, PaO2 60, HCO3 28.
CXR: hyperinflated, increased bronchovascular markings, no infiltrate.

ED course: nebulized albuterol and ipratropium x3, prednisone 40 mg, azithromycin 500 mg, supplemental oxygen titrated to 88 to 92%. Improved work of breathing.
Impression: acute exacerbation of COPD with acute respiratory acidosis.
Disposition: admitted to medicine.

documents.title: Discharge Summary, Medicine
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 03/16/2025, discharged 03/19/2025

Principal diagnosis: acute exacerbation of COPD.

Hospital course: Treated with scheduled nebulized bronchodilators, prednisone 40 mg daily and azithromycin. Did not require noninvasive ventilation. Weaned to room air by day 3, ambulating without desaturation at discharge. Lithium continued; renal function at his baseline. While in the ED he was approached by the research team about a study comparing a new bronchodilator with usual care for COPD exacerbations and said he was interested; no further information on enrollment in this record.

Discharge medications: complete prednisone 40 mg daily for a total of 5 days and azithromycin through day 5. Continue home tiotropium and albuterol as needed and all other home medications unchanged.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week. Smoking cessation counseled.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 09/15/2025 09:30, brought by his wife.

CC: confused and drowsy.

HPI: 58-year-old man with COPD and bipolar disorder. His wife says he has been increasingly sluggish over several days and this morning she found him confused, mumbling words she could not make out.
Meds: metoprolol tartrate, tiotropium, amlodipine, lisinopril, HCTZ, lithium, aspirin, atorvastatin. NKDA. Active smoker.

Vitals on arrival: BP 80/50, HR 45, RR 22, SpO2 92% RA.
Exam: drowsy, intermittently answers to name. Wheezes on lung exam. Extremities cool.
Fingerstick glucose 60. Lithium level 0.9.
ECG: sinus bradycardia, no ischemic changes.

Course: dextrose given. IV fluid boluses and atropine with no meaningful change in pressure or rate. Pill count by wife suggests extra metoprolol doses. Treated as beta-blocker toxicity: glucagon bolus and infusion, IV calcium, high-dose insulin with dextrose infusion, norepinephrine started. Toxicology consulted.
Impression: beta-blocker (metoprolol) overdose with bradycardia, hypotension and hypoglycemia.
Disposition: medical ICU.

documents.title: Discharge Summary, Medical ICU and Medicine
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 09/15/2025, discharged 09/19/2025

Diagnosis: metoprolol overdose, unintentional, with symptomatic bradycardia, hypotension and hypoglycemia.

Course: In the ICU on glucagon, high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy and norepinephrine. Heart rate and blood pressure recovered over the first day; norepinephrine off within 24 hours, insulin and glucagon weaned by day 2. Mental status back to baseline by day 2. Transferred to the floor day 3.
Once clear, he said he had been taking his morning metoprolol a second time on several days, without meaning to. Psychiatry consult: no suicidal ideation or intent, no current manic or depressive episode; lithium continued, level 0.9 on arrival.

Discharge medications: metoprolol tartrate resumed at 50 mg twice daily, observed tolerating it for 24 hours with stable HR and BP. All other home medications unchanged. Pharmacy to dispense in blister packs.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; outpatient psychiatry as scheduled.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Call from wife
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Patient's wife called (on his HIPAA form). He was brought to the regional hospital ED yesterday confused with a very slow heart rate and low pressure; she was told it was from too much metoprolol and he is in the ICU, more awake this morning. She wanted us to know. Routed to PCP. Will book a visit after discharge; asked her to bring all pill bottles.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Five days out from a 9/15 to 9/19 admission for metoprolol toxicity, ICU on glucagon, insulin and norepinephrine. Discharge summary received 9/22.

Came with his wife and every bottle. He does not remember the first day. He says he must have been taking the morning metoprolol twice some days. Psychiatry saw him inpatient, no concern for self-harm; he denies any thoughts of hurting himself today and his wife agrees he has been himself. Mood even.

Meds reconciled one by one at the table. Pharmacy has him in weekly blister packs now; wife checks the pack each night. Metoprolol back at 50 BID.

Exam: vitals charted, HR and BP fine on metoprolol. Alert, oriented, conversational. Lungs baseline. Heart regular. Warm extremities.

A/P:
1. Accidental metoprolol overdose, resolved. Blister packs and nightly check. Discussed calling us if he ever feels unsure whether he took a dose; skip rather than double.
2. Lithium: level 0.9 inpatient; repeat with BMP today.
3. Others unchanged.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Three vaccines today per PCP order: influenza (L deltoid), 2025-26 COVID (R deltoid), RSV single dose (L deltoid, separate site, an inch below). Wife present, she is checking his blister pack nightly. Observed 15 minutes.

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Dense airspace consolidation in the right lower lobe. Lungs otherwise hyperinflated without other focal opacity. No pneumothorax or large effusion. Heart size normal.

TECHNIQUE: CT angiography of the chest with IV contrast, arterial phase.
FINDINGS: Consolidation and ground-glass opacity in the right lower lobe with blood-density material in the right lower lobe segmental bronchi, consistent with aspirated blood. Enlarged, tortuous right bronchial artery. No pulmonary embolism. No endobronchial or parenchymal mass. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. No pleural effusion. Hyperinflated lungs.
reports.conclusion: Right lower lobe consolidation consistent with aspirated blood; enlarged right bronchial artery. No mass. No pulmonary embolism.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 11/25/2025 16:40

CC: coughing up blood.

59-year-old man with COPD, active smoking, and treated left oral tongue SCC with a left cervical nodal metastasis. Two hours of abrupt hemoptysis, bright red, about 100 mL by his estimate, still coughing up blood on arrival. No chest pain, no fever, no recent travel. Visibly anxious.
Meds per list: metoprolol tartrate, lisinopril, amlodipine, HCTZ, lithium, aspirin, atorvastatin, tiotropium. NKDA.

Vitals: BP 145/90, HR 98, RR 22, SpO2 92% RA.
Exam: reduced breath sounds with coarse crackles over the right lower lobe. Remainder unremarkable.
Labs: Hgb 13.2, WBC 9.0, plt 250, PT 12 s, INR 1.0, PTT 30 s, BUN 18, creatinine 2.0.
CXR: dense RLL consolidation.

Course: placed right side down, oxygen, IV tranexamic acid, aspirin held. CTA chest as above. Pulmonology and interventional radiology consulted.
Impression: massive hemoptysis, right lower lobe source.
Disposition: ICU.

documents.title: Discharge Summary, Pulmonary and Critical Care
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 11/25/2025, discharged 11/29/2025

Principal diagnosis: massive hemoptysis, right lower lobe.

Course:
- CT angiography: RLL consolidation consistent with aspirated blood, enlarged right bronchial artery, no mass, no PE.
- Bronchoscopy 11/25 evening: fresh blood and clot in the right lower lobe bronchi, cleared; no endobronchial lesion seen.
- Interventional radiology 11/26: right bronchial artery embolization, right common femoral access, without complication.
- No further hemoptysis after embolization. Hemoglobin stable. Aspirin resumed on day 3 with no recurrence.
- No other cause identified on this admission.

Discharge medications: home medications unchanged.
Follow-up: PCP in 1 week; pulmonology clinic with repeat CT chest in about 8 weeks.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Sean was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is Sean's wife on his account. He coughed up a lot of blood last Tuesday and was in the hospital until Saturday. They did a scope and blocked off an artery in his lung. He is home and has not coughed blood since. They said see you this week. Can we get in?

documents.title: RE: Sean was in the hospital
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Thank you for letting us know. We have him Friday 12/5 at 1:40. We have also requested the hospital records.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with wife after an 11/25 to 11/29 admission for massive hemoptysis. Hospital summary not here yet; history from them and the after-visit paperwork, which lists bronchoscopy and bronchial artery embolization. They were told no tumor was seen on the scope or the CT.

No blood since discharge. Cough back to his usual. No fever. Right groin access site healed. Took aspirin as instructed after discharge.

Exam: vitals charted. Breath sounds diminished both bases, no focal crackles today. Heart regular. Right femoral site clean, no hematoma.

A/P:
1. Hemoptysis, resolved after embolization. Pulmonology CT in late January. Call or go to the ED for any blood.
2. Smoking: told him plainly this is another reason. Pack a day still. Offered varenicline again; declined.
3. CBC, BMP and lithium today (quarterly draw due anyway).

reports.text:
TECHNIQUE: CT chest without contrast.
COMPARISON: CT angiography 11/25/2025.
FINDINGS: Previously seen right lower lobe consolidation and intrabronchial blood have resolved. Embolization material near the right bronchial artery origin. No pulmonary nodule or mass. No adenopathy. No effusion. Hyperinflated lungs.
reports.conclusion: Resolution of right lower lobe consolidation. No nodule or mass.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY CLINIC — FOLLOW-UP
Visit 01/22/2026

Seen 8 weeks after admission for massive hemoptysis from the right lower lobe, treated with right bronchial artery embolization. No recurrence of bleeding since. Breathing at his baseline. Still smoking about 1 pack daily.

CT chest today: RLL consolidation resolved; no nodule or mass.

Impression: hemoptysis without recurrence after embolization; no source lesion identified. COPD stable on tiotropium with albuterol as needed.

Plan: no further imaging needed for this unless bleeding recurs. Continue current inhalers. Smoking cessation once more strongly advised. Return as needed.

CC: primary care

documents.author: oncology

Visit 01/27/2026

Two years and three months after adjuvant radiation for pT1 N1 left oral tongue SCC. Hospitalized in November for hemoptysis; pulmonary CT last week clear of any mass, reviewed.
Exam: oral cavity and oropharynx without lesions. Neck without adenopathy. Laryngoscopy normal.

documents.title: Quarterly labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Stable creatinine, normal potassium, therapeutic lithium. Copy to psychiatry. Portal note sent.

reports.text: Obtained after return of spontaneous circulation. Sinus rhythm. No ST-segment elevation. No acute ST depression.

INDICATION: Out-of-hospital ventricular fibrillation arrest with return of circulation; known coronary artery disease.
ACCESS: right radial artery.
FINDINGS: Left main without significant disease. Left anterior descending with moderate 40% stenosis. Circumflex without significant disease. Right coronary artery with moderate 50% stenosis. No acute occlusion or thrombus. TIMI 3 flow in all vessels.
INTERVENTION: none.
reports.conclusion: Moderate non-obstructive coronary artery disease (LAD 40%, RCA 50%). No culprit lesion. No intervention.

reports.text: Left ventricle normal in size with low-normal systolic function, LVEF 50%. No regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricle normal size and function. No significant valvular disease. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: LVEF 50% without regional wall motion abnormality.

documents.title: Emergency Department and Resuscitation Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 03/30/2026 08:10 by EMS.

59-year-old man with CAD, COPD, a recent admission for massive hemoptysis and one last September for metoprolol overdose. Per bystanders at a train station he was holding his chest and seemed confused before he collapsed. Bystander CPR started right away; EMS AED delivered several shocks.

On arrival: unresponsive, pulseless, CPR in progress. Monitor: ventricular fibrillation. Bedside echo: no organized ventricular contraction.

Resuscitation: continued CPR, repeated defibrillation, epinephrine, amiodarone and then lidocaine for persistent VF. Return of spontaneous circulation after prolonged resuscitation. Intubated.
Post-ROSC ECG: sinus rhythm, no ST elevation.
Labs: potassium 3.9, magnesium 2.0, lithium 0.8.

Impression: out-of-hospital cardiac arrest from refractory ventricular fibrillation.
Disposition: emergent coronary angiography, then cardiac ICU.

documents.title: Discharge Summary, Cardiology
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — CARDIOLOGY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 03/30/2026, discharged 04/14/2026

Principal diagnosis: out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, refractory ventricular fibrillation.
Other: coronary artery disease, COPD, hypertension, CKD stage 3b from lithium, bipolar I disorder, treated oral tongue SCC.

Course:
- Coronary angiography 03/30: moderate non-obstructive disease (LAD 40%, RCA 50%), no acute occlusion, no intervention.
- Targeted temperature management for 24 hours in the cardiac ICU.
- High-sensitivity troponin I peaked at 2,460 ng/L, attributed to the arrest and resuscitation.
- Echo 04/01: LVEF 50%, no regional wall motion abnormality.
- Extubated day 3. Awake, oriented, following commands; no focal neurologic deficit.
- Lithium held while intubated and resumed on day 4; level 0.8 on arrival.
- No reversible cause identified. Single-chamber transvenous ICD implanted 04/10 via the left pectoral approach for secondary prevention. Device check before discharge normal.

Discharge medications: home medications unchanged (metoprolol tartrate 50 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, lithium 300 mg TID, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, tiotropium, albuterol as needed).
Activity: no lifting with left arm above shoulder for 4 weeks. No driving for 6 months.
Follow-up: device clinic in 4 to 6 weeks; PCP within 1 to 2 weeks.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Call from wife
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called crying. Sean collapsed at the train station yesterday morning, his heart stopped, strangers did CPR and the ambulance shocked him. He is in the cardiac ICU at the regional hospital on a breathing machine, and they are cooling him. Heart catheter yesterday, no stent. Told her we are so sorry, PCP will be told now. Asked her to call with updates and to have the hospital send records. PCP called her back at 9:10.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First visit since the VF arrest on 3/30 (admitted to 4/14). Discharge summary in since 4/16. Wife with him.

He remembers getting off the train and a tight chest, then nothing until a few days later in the ICU. Since home: tired, walking the block twice a day, no chest pain, no palpitations, no shocks from the device. Left chest incision sore but healing. Not driving, his wife drives. Mood: shaken, "lucky," sleeping ok. No thoughts of self-harm.

Recap: cath with moderate non-obstructive disease, no stent. EF 50%. No reversible cause found, single-chamber ICD 4/10. Neuro intact.

Meds: unchanged from before, confirmed with the blister pack and the bottles.

Exam: vitals charted. Alert, oriented, normal conversation and recall. Left pectoral device pocket clean, dry, no swelling. Heart regular. Lungs diminished with long expiration as before. No edema.

A/P:
1. Cardiac arrest from VF, survived neurologically intact, now with ICD. Device clinic follow-up next month. No driving until October per cardiology.
2. CAD: aspirin, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol continue.
3. Smoking: talked at length. Still a pack a day. Varenicline offered again with psychiatry in the loop; he will think on it.
4. Lithium: level and BMP today.
5. Wife given caregiver resources.

documents.title: Home device monitor
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called asking if we needed anything about the box the heart device company mailed him. Told him it is for remote checks with the device clinic and to call the number on the box for setup. He has his device clinic visit on 5/20.

documents.title: Device Clinic and Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY / DEVICE CLINIC
Visit 05/20/2026

Six weeks after single-chamber ICD implant for secondary prevention following a refractory VF arrest on 03/30/2026.
Symptoms: no syncope, no palpitations, no shocks.
Device interrogation: battery and lead parameters within normal limits; sensing and impedance stable. No ventricular arrhythmias recorded. No therapies delivered since implant.
Wound: well healed.
Plan: remote monitoring every 3 months; in-person device check in 6 months. Continue current medications. Driving restriction stands until October.

CC: primary care

documents.title: driving
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Is it really 6 months for driving? I feel fine and my wife is getting worn out driving me everywhere.

documents.title: RE: driving
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I know it is hard. After a cardiac arrest with a new defibrillator the 6 months comes from cardiology and the state guidance, and I agree with it. The date is around mid-October. Our office can help find a ride service for appointments if that would help your wife.

documents.title: lisinopril
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Blister pack pharmacy says they need a new lisinopril script.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months after the arrest. Getting stronger; walking 20 minutes most days. No chest pain, no fainting, no shocks. Device clinic in May was clean.
Breathing as usual, albuterol a couple of times a week. No blood in the sputum since November.
Mood stable, psychiatry last month, same lithium dose.
Blister packs going well, no missed or doubled doses that he or his wife know of.
Smoking: a pack a day. He says he tried and "couldn't."

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. Neck without nodes. Device site healed. Heart regular. Lungs diminished, long expiratory phase, no crackles. No edema.

A/P:
1. VF arrest survivor with ICD, CAD: stable. Cardiology following.
2. COPD: stable on tiotropium plus albuterol as needed.
3. CKD 3b from lithium, bipolar I: quarterly BMP and lithium today, CBC with it.
4. HTN: at goal.
5. Tongue SCC: NED, oncology visit later this month.
6. Tobacco: still 1 ppd. Offer stands.
RTC in about 3 months, or sooner.

documents.title: Labs from Friday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sean, kidney function is holding steady, potassium and sodium normal, blood count fine, lithium in range. Sent to your psychiatrist. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Head and Neck Surveillance Visit
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
HEAD AND NECK CLINIC
Visit 07/28/2026

Nearly three years after adjuvant radiation for pT1 N1 left oral tongue SCC. Interval cardiac arrest in March with ICD placement, recovering. No head and neck complaints.
Exam: oral cavity, oropharynx and neck without abnormality. Laryngoscopy without lesions.
Impression: no evidence of disease.
Plan: continue visits every 6 months.

CC: primary care
